title: Changes-in-Changes for Ordered Choice Models with Underreporting
abstract: arXiv:2401.00618v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We develop a Difference-in-Differences framework for discrete, ordered outcomes subject to underreporting. Such outcomes commonly arise in self-reported surveys on socially undesirable or stigmatized behaviors, where respondents may conceal their true behavior. For a discrete Changes-in-Changes model that is shown to admit an equivalent threshold-crossing representation, we derive nonparametric bounds for the counterfactual and factual outcome distributions as well as for the associated quantile treatment effects when outcomes are underreported. These bounds are shown to be sharp uniformly across outcome levels under additional support conditions, and we propose suitable estimation and bootstrap inference procedures. In an extension, we also consider a semiparametric underreporting model that allows to point identify and estimate distributional treatment effects. As an application, we investigate the impact of recreational marijuana

translated_title: 存在瞒报的有序选择模型的“变化中的变化”（Changes-in-Changes）方法
translated_abstract: 我们为受瞒报影响的离散有序结果开发了一个双重差分框架。这类结果常见于涉及社会不良或污名化行为的自我报告调查中，受访者可能会隐瞒其真实行为。对于一个被证明具有等价阈值跨越表示的离散“变化中的变化”模型，我们推导出了当结果被瞒报时，反事实与实际结果分布以及相关分位数处理效应的非参数边界。在额外的支撑条件下，这些边界被证明在所有结果水平上均为一致紧致，并且我们提出了合适的估计方法和自助法（bootstrap）推断程序。作为扩展，我们还考虑了一个半参数瞒报模型，该模型能够对分布处理效应进行点识别和估计。作为应用，我们研究了娱乐性大麻（使用所受的影响）……
tldr: 本文针对自我报告调查中常见的瞒报问题，为离散有序结果建立了双重差分分析框架，推导出反事实分布及分位数处理效应的紧致非参数边界，并以娱乐性大麻使用为应用实例。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a Difference-in-Differences framework for discrete ordered outcomes subject to underreporting, deriving sharp nonparametric bounds for counterfactual distributions and quantile treatment effects, with an application to recreational marijuana use.
